vulnerability.title: Disable Accepting Router Advertisements on all IPv6 Interfaces by Default
vulnerability.description: To set the runtime status of the net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra kernel parameter, run the following command: $ sudo sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 To make sure that the setting is persistent, add the following line to a file in the directory /etc/sysctl.d: net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra = 0
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if rpm --quiet -q kernel-core; then # Comment out any occurrences of net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra from /etc/sysctl.d/*.conf files for f in /etc/sysctl.d/*.conf /run/sysctl.d/*.conf /usr/local/lib/sysctl.d/*.conf; do # skip systemd-sysctl symlink (/etc/sysctl.d/99-sysctl.conf -> /etc/sysctl.conf) if [[ "$(readlink -f "$f")" == "/etc/sysctl.conf" ]]; then continue; fi matching_list=$(grep -P '^(?!#).*[\s]*net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra.*$' $f | uniq ) if ! test -z "$matching_list"; then while IFS= read -r entry; do escaped_entry=$(sed -e 's|/|\\/|g' <<< "$entry") # comment out "net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra" matches to preserve user data sed -i --follow-symlinks "s/^${escaped_entry}$/# &/g" $f done <<< "$matching_list" fi done # # S

triage_decision.reason: Disabling IPv6 router advertisements via a sysctl setting is a standard hardening practice that does not affect authentication, authorization, or critical services such as SSH. The change is local to the kernel networking stack and can be applied safely without risk of lockout.

reasoning_messages.reasoning:
We must follow plan: we need to first plan description to submit for review with review_plan. Plan: modify sysctl setting. Steps: read /etc/sysctl.conf? but recommended to use /etc/sysctl.d/99-sysctl.conf? Actually default config may be /etc/sysctl.d/99-sysctl.conf. We should add line "net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra = 0" in a file under /etc/sysctl.d/ e.g., 10-networking-sysctl.conf or like /etc/sysctl.d/99-disable-ra.conf. But must not duplicate existing lines. Let's inspect if /etc/sysctl.d/*.conf already have that setting. Use read_file to check each file. But we can't find all. We simply create a file /etc/sysctl.d/10-disable-RA.conf with the setting, ensuring not duplicate. If already present, modify existing. Approach: use grep -q to find. But we must use run_cmd. We'll need to supply commands one: first read all files maybe too many. But rule says only one command at a time. We'll first read through all config files to determine if the setting exists: we can run a command to list files and check if any contain the string. But easier: create new file with the setting; any duplication is fine as long as didn't set duplicate? But duplicate entries may still work? But to avoid duplicate lines: we can write file with the line and no duplicates likely.

Thus plan: create /etc/sysctl.d/10-disable-RA.conf containing "net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra = 0". Then reload sysctl. Use run_cmd 'sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0' to set runtime.

review_feedback: The script only comments out any existing net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra lines but does not actually set the value to 0, so the vulnerability remains unmitigated. It also lacks a runtime sysctl command and a persistent configuration entry. The absence of a proper set command can lead to incomplete remediation.

concerns: Vulnerability is not addressed - accept_ra may stay 1 (default).
Potential for confusion if other scripts modify the same setting.
suggested_improvements: Append a line 'net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra = 0' to a new file in /etc/sysctl.d/, e.g., /etc/sysctl.d/99-disable-ra.conf.
After file update, run 'sudo sysctl -p /etc/sysctl.d/99-disable-ra.conf' or 'sudo sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0' to enforce at runtime.
Ensure script checks for readonly systems or already set value before commenting.
Add error handling for missing directories or permission issues.
